analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (the `Traffic:` description in `darkbloom status`, with head units covering later sections) and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (the `coordinator traffic` doctor row at line 83 and the re-registration row at line 143). No executable code, keys, endpoints, crypto, or authorization logic is modified.

The documented behavior changes are: (1) traffic eligibility is now judged from current evidence only; (2) a request the coordinator routed after its latest status counts as eligible (`coordinator_connection.last_request_at`); (3) a refusal counts only for 60 seconds (`refusalMaxAge`); (4) a new `unconfirmed` informational state; and (5) re-registration triggers only while the verdict stays `NOT receiving`, so a single refusal at registration does not trigger it.

Security-relevant reading against the threat model:
- T-053 and T-052: the docs say a routed request makes the provider show as eligible. This is a local diagnostic and recovery heuristic, not a serving authorization. The coordinator's grant/lease and EvaluateAuthorization remain authoritative, and the docs do not say the provider self-authorizes. The text is consistent with the platform-owned authorization boundary.
- T-057 (availability): less aggressive re-registration, and no re-registration after a one-time refusal, are documented. Whether the real code matches is outside the supplied evidence, since the Swift sources (ServingReadiness.swift, UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift) are not in this batch. This is a documentation-to-code consistency question, not a verified regression.
- A-018: the add-on hold skip text is unchanged.
- T-058: the new `unconfirmed` state avoids stating exclusion falsely, which improves diagnostic accuracy. The docs do not leak identifiers.

The remaining unchanged documentation in cli-reference.md (the token path, the add-on runtime files, the cache variables, the worker opt-in) is pre-existing, and I raise no new issue on it. The patch excerpt for cli-reference.md was truncated, so I could not verify the remainder of that hunk. The visible head text for the Traffic bullet falls outside the supplied numbered range, so no line citation was possible. I found no concrete security regression.
